findings.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing exit-code consumers; FEATURE_DISABLED=4 reuses the old recreate value, causing callers to misclassify 'feature disabled' as 'recreate upgrade required' and potentially shut down the deployment
Docs table appends exit 4 with new semantics without flagging the renumbering of 4→3

Feature gate uses Profile.isFeatureEnabled before the CLI has parsed/started the profile, so it may read the persisted build-time profile incorrectly and report the feature as disabled even when passed via --features
Operator path: if the feature is enabled only via CR/FeatureSpec without rebuilding the image, the compatibility check exits FEATURE_DISABLED and the operator does not distinguish exit code 4 from 3
Test expectation flipped from assertError("Missing required argument") to assertNoMessage for testMissingOptionOnSave, masking a potential required-argument validation regression
printFeatureDisabled errors are routed through the error printer but the command exits via picocli.exit(4), a non-standard picocli exit code, which generic picocli tooling may misinterpret

CompatibilityResult.java silently changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and reuses 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking external automation/scripts (and the Operator per update-compatibility.adoc:124-135) that key on exit code 4 = "recreate required" — a feature-disabled exit (4) will be misinterpreted as recreate upgrade required (P2 correctness/compat concern)

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult.java, with 4 repurposed as FEATURE_DISABLED; existing automation treating exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will silently misinterpret it as 'feature disabled', risking the wrong upgrade strategy (rolling instead of recreate) being applied — a behavioral contract change with no migration note

testFeatureNotEnabled may never reach the feature check because picocli validates required options (e.g., OUTPUT_OPTION_NAME) before run() is invoked, so the process exits with a usage error before Profile.isFeatureEnabled is evaluated and printFeatureDisabled is never printed, making the test flaky or masking actual behavior

Feature-disabled exit path calls picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) from inside run() rather than throwing, bypassing the command's normal exception-to-exit-code mapping and creating an inconsistent, undocumented exit code (4) that collides with the historical meaning of 4; exit-code semantics should be documented in CLI help text

Behavioral change of exit codes (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE 4→3, 4 reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED) in CompatibilityResult.java:31-34 is a breaking change for automation with no test coverage verifying either new exit code; UpdateCommandDistTest.testWrongVersions asserts only the error message, not the exit code

testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest.java:47-51 has weak assertions: only checks the error string instead of the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), and doesn't exercise UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata as separate invocations

No integration test verifies the operator failure path when the rolling-updates feature is disabled, despite docs claiming the operator will fail; all existing upgrade tests enable the feature and silently skip the disabled-feature scenario

Docs/tests divergence: update-compatibility.adoc:128-135 documents exit code 4 as feature disabled, but no test or doc table asserts that disabled-feature and recreate paths produce different codes (3 vs 4); an e2e test executing the docs' exit-code table would prevent drift

Exit-code remapping in CompatibilityResult.java changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and repurposes 4 as FEATURE_DISABLED without migrating any consumers, so scripts parsing exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will misclassify or treat new code 3 as unknown error and fail the upgrade path

Docs (advanced-configuration.adoc, update-compatibility.adoc) claim operator enforcement of the disabled feature but the diff contains no operator runtime code checking ROLLING_UPDATES or mapping the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code — documented guard is not implemented

testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest.java only asserts the error string and does not assert the exit code, so a failure to propagate picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) would still pass the test while the command exits 0

Feature check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java / UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java runs before validateConfig(), so a user with both a wrong config and the feature disabled only sees the feature message and hits the config error on a second run

UpgradeTest enables the feature only on the initial deployment; invoking update-compatibility on an older Keycloak pod that predates the ROLLING_UPDATES feature yields FEATURE_DISABLED (4), which an exit-code-interpreting operator misclassifies as 'recreate required' — no handling for old servers that don't know the feature

adjudication_records.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing exit-code consumers; FEATURE_DISABLED=4 reuses the old recreate value, causing callers to misclassify 'feature disabled' as 'recreate upgrade required' and potentially shut down the deployment

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (quarkus/runtime/.../CompatibilityResult.java). That is a behavior/API contract change for process exit codes. While the new mapping may be intentional (comment references picocli exit codes), it is still a potentially breaking change for any external scripts/tools that previously interpreted exit code `4` as "recreate upgrade required"—they would now misclassify `FEATURE_DISABLED` as recreate unless updated. The diff does not show any internal consumer breakage, but the compatibility concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Docs table appends exit 4 with new semantics without flagging the renumbering of 4→3

Feature gate uses Profile.isFeatureEnabled before the CLI has parsed/started the profile, so it may read the persisted build-time profile incorrectly and report the feature as disabled even when passed via --features

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a feature gate at the start of `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` / `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` using `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)`. However, picocli parses CLI arguments before invoking `run()`, and the accompanying dist tests were updated to pass `--features=rolling-updates` (e.g., `@Launch({... , ENABLE_FEATURE})` and `distribution.run(..., ENABLE_FEATURE)`) and then assert subsequent behavior (like missing required args) rather than the new "feature not enabled" error. If the feature flag from `--features` were not visible at `run()` time, those updated tests would fail by hitting the early exit instead. Nothing in the diff shows profile initialization happening after `run()` is called.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Operator path: if the feature is enabled only via CR/FeatureSpec without rebuilding the image, the compatibility check exits FEATURE_DISABLED and the operator does not distinguish exit code 4 from 3

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `update-compatibility`/`update-compatibility check` now hard-fail with exit code `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4) when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled, and it changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3. However, the finding asserts specific Operator behavior (enabling only via CR/FeatureSpec without rebuilding the image, and the Operator not distinguishing exit code 4 vs 3). This diff does not include any Operator implementation that invokes the compatibility check or interprets these exit codes, so that Operator-path claim cannot be verified from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test expectation flipped from assertError("Missing required argument") to assertNoMessage for testMissingOptionOnSave, masking a potential required-argument validation regression

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `testMissingOptionOnSave` is updated to launch with `--features=rolling-updates` and then asserts `assertNoMessage("Missing required argument")`. There is no evidence in this diff that the test previously asserted `assertError("Missing required argument")`, nor that a required-argument validation is being masked. The paired `testMissingOptionOnCheck` still asserts the missing required input argument error for the `check` subcommand, suggesting the intent is to ensure `metadata` doesn’t require that argument once the feature gate is satisfied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: printFeatureDisabled errors are routed through the error printer but the command exits via picocli.exit(4), a non-standard picocli exit code, which generic picocli tooling may misinterpret

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces a dedicated exit code for the new condition (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4) and uses picocli.exit(...) accordingly in UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata. Picocli does not restrict applications to only its predefined ExitCode constants; custom exit codes are valid. The claim that exit code 4 is “non-standard” in a way that generic picocli tooling would misinterpret is speculative and not evidenced by the diff (and the diff even documents 1/2 as picocli-reserved examples while choosing 3/4 for app-specific meanings).

adjudication_records.issue_text: CompatibilityResult.java silently changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and reuses 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking external automation/scripts (and the Operator per update-compatibility.adoc:124-135) that key on exit code 4 = "recreate required" — a feature-disabled exit (4) will be misinterpreted as recreate upgrade required (P2 correctness/compat concern)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (CompatibilityResult.java). This is a backwards-incompatible behavioral change for consumers that previously interpreted exit code 4 as “recreate required”. The docs are updated to add a new meaning for code 4 (feature disabled) but the diff does not show any compatibility layer or retention of the old recreate exit code, so existing automation keyed on 4 would misinterpret results.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the upgrade exit code semantics changed (4→3, with 4 repurposed) and explicitly notes this is a behavioral contract change lacking a migration note, which aligns with the golden requirement to add changelog/release notes and guidance for the exit code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled may never reach the feature check because picocli validates required options (e.g., OUTPUT_OPTION_NAME) before run() is invoked, so the process exits with a usage error before Profile.isFeatureEnabled is evaluated and printFeatureDisabled is never printed, making the test flaky or masking actual behavior

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `testFeatureNotEnabled` launches `UpdateCompatibility` + `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` with no additional options. The PR adds the feature gate inside `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` (and `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()`), and the only subcommand shown elsewhere to have a required option is `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` (tested via `INPUT_OPTION_NAME`). The PR’s own test `testMissingOptionOnSave` runs `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` without `OUTPUT_OPTION_NAME` and explicitly asserts there is no “Missing required argument”, which strongly implies `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` does not have required options that would prevent `run()` from executing. Therefore the claimed pre-run picocli validation blocking the feature check (and preventing `printFeatureDisabled`) is not supported by what this diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-disabled exit path calls picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) from inside run() rather than throwing, bypassing the command's normal exception-to-exit-code mapping and creating an inconsistent, undocumented exit code (4) that collides with the historical meaning of 4; exit-code semantics should be documented in CLI help text

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an early-exit path using `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` inside `run()` (in both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata`), but the finding’s key claims aren’t supported: (1) there is no verifiable “collision” with the historical meaning of exit code 4 because the diff explicitly changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`; (2) exit code 4 is documented in the updated guide table (`update-compatibility.adoc` adds result 4: feature disabled); and (3) the diff does not show any existing “normal exception-to-exit-code mapping” that would be bypassed, so that part is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change of exit codes (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE 4→3, 4 reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED) in CompatibilityResult.java:31-34 is a breaking change for automation with no test coverage verifying either new exit code; UpdateCommandDistTest.testWrongVersions asserts only the error message, not the exit code

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes exit-code constants in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` 4→3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`). In `UpdateCommandDistTest`, only the compatible path asserts an exit code (`assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())`), while the new feature-disabled path (`testFeatureNotEnabled`) asserts only the error text and the recreate/incompatible paths (e.g., `testWrongVersions`) also assert only error messages, not exit codes. So the finding that this behavioral change is unverified by tests is grounded in the diff; it’s a potentially breaking interface/contract change, but not demonstrably a defect in this PR by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest.java:47-51 has weak assertions: only checks the error string instead of the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), and doesn't exercise UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata as separate invocations

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavior: both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata now exit early when Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES is disabled and call picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) (value 4). However, UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and does not assert the exit code, nor does it cover the UpdateCompatibilityCheck path without the feature enabled (it only launches UpdateCompatibility + UpdateCompatibilityMetadata in a single invocation). This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test verifies the operator failure path when the rolling-updates feature is disabled, despite docs claiming the operator will fail; all existing upgrade tests enable the feature and silently skip the disabled-feature scenario

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new preview feature `ROLLING_UPDATES` and documentation explicitly warns that the Operator will fail if `rolling-updates` is not enabled. However, the only Operator-related integration test change (`operator/.../UpgradeTest.java`) now explicitly enables the feature via `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`, and there is no corresponding Operator integration test exercising the disabled-feature/failure path. While CLI dist tests cover the disabled-feature case for update-compatibility commands, no Operator failure-path test is present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Docs/tests divergence: update-compatibility.adoc:128-135 documents exit code 4 as feature disabled, but no test or doc table asserts that disabled-feature and recreate paths produce different codes (3 vs 4); an e2e test executing the docs' exit-code table would prevent drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces distinct exit codes in `CompatibilityResult` (`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3`, `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`) and documents feature-disabled as exit code 4 in `update-compatibility.adoc` (adds `m|4 ... feature 'rolling-updates' is disabled`). However, the added/modified dist tests (`UpdateCommandDistTest`) only assert the error message for the feature-disabled path (`testFeatureNotEnabled`) and do not assert the exit code; similarly, no shown test asserts the recreate-path exit code. This is a concrete gap that could allow doc/code drift without failing tests, but it is not a currently verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exit-code remapping in CompatibilityResult.java changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and repurposes 4 as FEATURE_DISABLED without migrating any consumers, so scripts parsing exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will misclassify or treat new code 3 as unknown error and fail the upgrade path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does intentionally remap exit codes in `CompatibilityResult` (RECREATE 4→3, new `FEATURE_DISABLED=4`) and updates at least some in-repo consumers/docs/tests to reflect the new meaning (e.g., `UpdateCompatibilityCheck/Metadata` now `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` and docs add an `m|4` row for feature-disabled). The claim that this happens “without migrating any consumers” is not supported by the diff, but the finding’s core concern—breaking backward compatibility for external scripts parsing exit code 4—is a real, diff-grounded compatibility/contract issue rather than an immediate functional defect shown in the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Docs (advanced-configuration.adoc, update-compatibility.adoc) claim operator enforcement of the disabled feature but the diff contains no operator runtime code checking ROLLING_UPDATES or mapping the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code — documented guard is not implemented

adjudication.rationale: The diff does implement a guard for the update-compatibility CLI commands: `UpdateCompatibilityCheck` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata` now check `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)`, print an explicit error via `printFeatureDisabled()`, and exit with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (new exit code 4). The docs’ cautions can be consistent with this behavior (commands/operator workflows failing when the feature is disabled) without requiring additional operator-controller/runtime checks in this diff. The finding’s claim that the documented guard is “not implemented” is therefore not supported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest.java only asserts the error string and does not assert the exit code, so a failure to propagate picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) would still pass the test while the command exits 0

adjudication.rationale: In `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled`, the test only calls `cliResult.assertError("Unable to use this command...")` and does not explicitly assert the process exit code. The production code paths in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` / `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` call `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` when `ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled, so an explicit exit-code assertion would better verify that behavior. The diff does not show whether `CLIResult.assertError(...)` implicitly checks for a non-zero exit code, so the finding is about test completeness rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java / UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java runs before validateConfig(), so a user with both a wrong config and the feature disabled only sees the feature message and hits the config error on a second run

adjudication.rationale: In both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(), the new guard `if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)) { ... return; }` is placed before `validateConfig()`, so a misconfigured run will be short-circuited with only the feature-disabled message and no config validation until the feature is enabled. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/diagnostics ordering concern, but the diff also intentionally makes the command unusable without the preview feature (docs and tests expect this), so it’s not clearly a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UpgradeTest enables the feature only on the initial deployment; invoking update-compatibility on an older Keycloak pod that predates the ROLLING_UPDATES feature yields FEATURE_DISABLED (4), which an exit-code-interpreting operator misclassifies as 'recreate required' — no handling for old servers that don't know the feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new exit code `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` and makes `update-compatibility` commands exit with that code when `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` is not enabled. However, the claimed operator misclassification of exit code 4 as “recreate required” is not shown anywhere in this diff, and the scenario about invoking the command on an “older Keycloak pod that predates the feature” cannot be verified from the provided changes (no operator-side exit-code interpretation logic is included). The statement about `UpgradeTest` only enabling the feature on the initial deployment is true (it sets `FeatureSpec.enabledFeatures` in `createInitialDeployment`), but the rest of the finding goes beyond what the diff demonstrates.
